metadata.title: An open-source package for low-frequency reconstruction based on 3D convolutional neural networks
metadata.description:
An open-source package for low-frequency reconstruction based on 3D convolutional neural networks

Copyright

This package includes all the codes related to the work presented in "An open-source package for low-frequency reconstruction based on 3D convolutional neural networks". This package is free. You can redistribute it and/or modify it for research purpose only. For the commercial license, please contact the authors (xtchai@126.com).

If you think the codes are helpful, please cite the following related works.

Xintao Chai, Genyang Tang, Kai Lin, Zhe Yan, Hanming Gu, Ronghua Peng, Xiaodong Sun, and Wenjun Cao, (2021), "Deep learning for multitrace sparse-spike deconvolution" GEOPHYSICS, 86(3): V207-V218, doi: 10.1190/geo2020-0342.1.
Xintao Chai, Genyang Tang, Shangxu Wang, Kai Lin, and Ronghua Peng (2021).  "Deep Learning for Irregularly and Regularly Missing 3-D Data Reconstruction", IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, doi: 10.1109/TGRS.2020.3016343. 
Xintao Chai, Genyang Tang, Shangxu Wang, Ronghua Peng, Wei Chen, and Jingnan Li (2020). "Deep Learning for Regularly Missing Data Reconstruction", IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 58(6), 4406-4423, doi: 10.1109/TGRS.2020.2963928. 
Xintao Chai, Hanming Gu, Feng Li, Hongyou Duan, Xiaobo Hu, and Kai Lin (2020). "Deep learning for irregularly and regularly missing data reconstruction", Scientific Reports, 10, doi: 10.1038/s41598-020-59801-x.
Xintao Chai, Taihui Yang, Junyong Yu, Wenhui Nie, Kai Lin, Genyang Tang, Xiaodong Sun, Wenjun Cao, and Cheng Yuan, (2021), "An open-source package for low-frequency reconstruction based on 3D convolutional neural networks" , submitted to Geophysical Journal International.
Xintao Chai, Wenhui Nie, Taihui Yang, Junyong Yu, Kai Lin, Genyang Tang, Xinyue Liu, Wenjun Cao, and Xiaodong Sun, (2021), "An open-source package for machine-learning-based seismic facies classification: Benchmarking experiments on the SEG 2020 open data", submitted to Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth.

The corresponding LaTeX bibliography file LaTeX.bib is also enclosed for your convenience.

Copyright (C) 2021 Xintao Chai's Team

Requirements

  • Keras==2.3.0
  • tensorflow-gpu==1.15.0
  • pandas==0.23.4
  • segyio==1.9.6
  • python 3.7.9

Data

The derived data and results related to this work are uploaded to Zenodo and are freely available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4729995.

  • The raw Marmousi2 open data set is available at this link.
  • The raw Mobil Avo Viking Graben Line 12 open data set is available at this link.
  • The raw marine data set from the Gulf of Mexico is available at this link.

Run

  1. Create folders and transfer the download files
    Models produced by training and data used during training and testing will be saved in the following path. If you want to change it, please edit config.txt.

    module_data_dir = 'D:/BigData/AI_LowFrequencyReconstruction'

    After download the derived data and results, you need to make some changes to AI_LFR_0.py:

    data_path = r'PATH_1'
results_path = r'PATH_2'

    The PATH_1 should contains raw_data and test_data folders, and the PATH_2 should ends with 'paper_results'.

    AI_LFR_0.py

  2. Make training and validation data

    AI_LFR3D_1_data_maker.py
AI_LFR2D_1_data_maker.py

  3. Train model

    AI_LFR3D_2_train_task_kernel_size.py
AI_LFR2D_2_train_task.py

  4. Test model

    AI_LFR3D_3_test_a_sample.py
AI_LFR3D_3_test_a_sample_all_models.py
AI_LFR2D_3_test_all_samples_mob_gom.py
AI_LFR2D_3_test_all_samples_val.py

  5. Produce figures

    figure02_training_demo.m
figure03_training_logs.m
figures04_05_validation.m
figure06_kernel.m
figure07_Mobil_data.m
figure08_GoM_data.m

metadata.title: unet-acquisition-footprint
metadata.description:
Mitigating Acquisition Footprints in Time-Lapse Seismic Data

Code, trained weights and reproduction notebooks for:

Ahmad, A.B., Tsuji, T., Kioka, A., Kimura, T., Xu, S. Mitigating Acquisition Footprints in Time-Lapse Seismic Data: A U-Net Reconstruction Approach for Consistent Monitoring. Earth Systems and Environment (under review).

A U-Net is trained to map sparse, irregularly acquired monitor surveys onto a dense baseline grid, so that 4D differences reflect subsurface change rather than acquisition geometry. The distinguishing element is upstream of the network: training pairs are built by perturbing source coordinates in the continuous spatial domain before solving the wave equation, rather than by decimating traces from a precomputed dense grid. The network therefore learns to invert real wavefield distortion (NMO stretch, wavelet interference, fold loss) instead of filling digital gaps.

Repository layout

.
├── notebooks/
│   ├── 01_main_workflow.ipynb            End-to-end: modeling → preprocessing → training → evaluation
│   ├── 02_ablation_data_generation.ipynb Physics-based scattering vs. post-hoc decimation (3×3 cross-test)
│   ├── 03_ablation_capacity.ipynb        16 / 32 / 64 / 128 base-filter comparison
│   ├── 04_velocity_sensitivity.ipynb     NMO velocity error of 0, ±5, ±10 percent
│   ├── 05_perturbation_scale.ipynb       Source mispositioning from field-realistic to stress-test scale
│   └── 06_conventional_baselines.ipynb   U-Net vs. F-K filtering and horizontal regularization
├── models/
│   └── unet_32filters.keras              Trained weights for the reported model
├── data/velocity_models/                 Input velocity models (see Data below)
├── outputs/                              Generated stacks, figures and logs (not tracked)
├── requirements.txt
└── LICENSE
 

Installation

Python 3.11, CUDA 12.4. A GPU is required for forward modeling and training; inference with the released weights runs on CPU.

git clone https://github.com/<ORG>/<REPO>.git
cd <REPO>
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
 

The pipeline deliberately spans two frameworks: PyTorch and Deepwave for wave propagation and pre-processing, TensorFlow/Keras for the network. Both will try to claim GPU memory on import. If you hit an out-of-memory error, restart the kernel between the modeling stage (notebook 01, sections 1 to 3) and the training stage (sections 4 onward), reloading the cached stacks from outputs/stacked/.

Data

The three CCS time-lapse velocity models (baseline.bin, monitoring_stage1.bin, monitoring_stage2.bin) go in data/velocity_models/. They are raw float32, shaped 601 × 501 (nx × nz) at 2 m grid spacing. Monitoring stages carry a CO₂ plume introduced as a Gaussian-smoothed perturbation of −25 percent Vp, +2 percent Vs and −5 percent density over the injection interval.

The Marmousi2 model used for the generalization test is available from the Allied Geophysical Laboratories.

Reproducing the reported results

Run notebooks/01_main_workflow.ipynb top to bottom. Section 5 retrains from scratch; skip it and run section 6 to load the released weights instead.

The reported model is trained on the monitoring stage 1 pair (stack_mon1_bad as input, stack_mon1_good as target). Key configuration:

Parameter Value
Grid spacing dx 2 m
Time step dt 0.004 s
Samples nt 300
Ricker dominant frequency 25 Hz
Receivers per shot 300
Shots, dense target 100, no perturbation
Shots, degraded input see notebook 01, section 2
Patch size 128 × 128
Sliding-window step 5
Train / validation / test 70 / 21 / 9 percent, random_state = 42
Base filters 32
Loss Mean absolute error
Optimizer Adam, learning rate tuned by Hyperband, gradient clipping 1.0
Batch size 32
Hardware NVIDIA RTX A6000, 47 GB

Online augmentation (horizontal flip, small rotation, small translation, and Gaussian noise on the input only) is applied per batch, so no two epochs see identical patches.

Random seeds

GLOBAL_SEED = 42 is set at the top of every notebook, covering Python's random, NumPy, PyTorch (including CUDA) and TensorFlow. This seeds the stochastic source scattering, the train/validation/test split and the augmentation stream, so the reported training data and splits regenerate exactly.

One deliberate exception: the generalization checks re-run forward modeling with a fresh random source distribution, which is the point of the test. Those cells are marked in the notebooks. Re-running them gives a new realization each time and metrics will move by a percentage point or two.

Metrics

Three metrics are used, and values are not comparable across evaluation contexts:

  • NRMS (Kragh and Christie, 2002), computed globally over the full stacked section with no sub-windowing. Lower is better; below 10 percent is conventionally considered reliable for 4D interpretation.
  • SSIM, on the reconstructed section or on the time-lapse difference map depending on context.
  • Reconstruction accuracy, the percentage of samples within an absolute tolerance of 0.01 of the target.

Each notebook prints which context it is reporting.

Citation

@article{ahmad2026footprint,
  title  = {Mitigating Acquisition Footprints in Time-Lapse Seismic Data:
            A U-Net Reconstruction Approach for Consistent Monitoring},
  author = {Ahmad, Ahmad Bahaa and Tsuji, Takeshi and Kioka, Arata and
            Kimura, Toshinori and Xu, Shibo},
  journal = {Earth Systems and Environment},
  year   = {2026},
  note   = {Under review}
}
 

Archived release: [DOI to be added on acceptance]

MIT. See LICENSE.

Acknowledgements

Built on Deepwave (Richardson, 2020) for wave propagation. Supported by the Ministry of the Environment of Japan ("Environmentally conscious CCUS integrated experimental site and supply chain construction") and JSPS KAKENHI JP24H00440.

metadata.title: Marmousi2-Res: Multi-Saturation Resistivity Extension to the Marmousi2 Model
metadata.description:
Marmousi2-Res is a resistivity companion to the Marmousi2 elastic benchmark, derived from its elastic properties using Gassmann fluid substitution and Archie's law. The model is classified into seven lithologies at the pixel level, and porosity is recovered for all ten hydrocarbon zones by back-calculating from the Gassmann equation and the density relation. Resistivity is calculated from Archie's equation using temperature-corrected brine resistivity from the Arps relation.

The release provides resistivity grids for six uniform water saturations (Sw = 15% to 100%) and two split-saturation scenarios with distinct gas- and oil-zone saturations. The mean P-wave velocity error after round-trip fluid substitution is 4 m/s (<0.4%), and the recovered matrix density is constrained to 2.56-2.62 g/cm3. Averaged over all zones, resistivity is approximately 263 times more sensitive than P-wave velocity to a saturation change from 30% to 70% hydrocarbon saturation. One-dimensional CSEM modelling shows that reservoirs buried 600-1600 m below the seafloor are detectable with standard marine CSEM acquisition, while the deepest zones at approximately 2500 m are marginally detectable at low frequency.

This archive contains the pixel-level lithology classification, hydrocarbon-zone masks, resistivity grids for all saturation scenarios, rock-physics tables, and all scripts required to reproduce the workflow, including the 1D CSEM detectability analysis.

Licensing. The Python source code is released under the MIT License. The generated data products are released under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0). The bundled Dipole1D forward-modelling code (Key, 2009), located in scripts/csem_detectability/dipole1d, is redistributed under its own GPL-3 license; see the COPYING file in that directory.

This archive supports the article published in Applied Computing and Geosciences (Elsevier).

metadata.title: Code and frozen results for "Global-to-Local Decoding for Full-Waveform Inversion with Missing Low Frequencies" (MR-ASPD-FWI)
metadata.description:
This archive contains the complete source code and the frozen numerical results supporting the manuscript "Global-to-Local Decoding for Full-Waveform Inversion with Missing Low Frequencies" (MR-ASPD-FWI), submitted to Geophysical Prospecting.

The work addresses cycle skipping in full-waveform inversion when the lowest usable seismic frequencies are absent and the initial velocity model is poor. It develops a global-to-local, multi-resolution active-set pruning-decoding method that seeks a basin-entered initial model for subsequent continuous waveform inversion rather than replacing it: multi-shot coherent localization supplies recall, nonlinear list generation preserves hypotheses, and support pruning with an explicit zero state supplies precision.

The archive includes the two-dimensional acoustic finite-difference solver, the block-parameterized inversion machinery, the MR-ASPD decoder, every experiment driver (convergence basin, frequency sweep, noise and off-grid validations, randomized-placement stress test, faulted-layered surface-seismic case, public Marmousi2-background monitoring replication, optimal-transport and adjoint baselines, and the end-to-end handoff to continuous FWI), all figure-generation scripts, and the frozen result tables and logs from which every number in the manuscript is taken. A reproducibility manifest maps each reported result, table, and figure to the exact script and frozen output that produced it.

All observations are synthetic; no field or proprietary data are included. The public Marmousi2 P-wave velocity model used as a background is third-party CC-BY material and is not redistributed here; its source, licence, and processing protocol are recorded in the manifest.
